clusters.text: US Coast Guard said crews had so far found the cabin of the plane, a life raft and three life jackets Rescue crews were searching for six people on board a small plane that crashed Tuesday afternoon off the coast of Mississippi . Crews have so far found three life jackets, a life raft and the cabin of the plane. The plane’s cabin was floating on the water, Juan Ros, a US Coast Guard spokesperson, said. The plane, a Cessna 210, went down around 3.30pm in the Gulf of Mexico between Pascagoula, Mississippi, and Horn Island, which is part of the Gulf Islands national seashore. There were four adults and two boys, ages eight and 10, on board, authorities said. The Cessna was en route from New Orleans to Fort Meyers, Florida, according to the flight tracking website FlightAware. According to the Coast Guard, the plane was descending at a rate of 10,000ft per minute when contact was lost. The Federal Aviation Administration and the National Transportation Safety Board, which will investigate the crash, said on Tuesday they were aware of it.

Islamabad, Pakistan — It was 5:18am (00:18 GMT) on Wednesday, before dawn in a chilly Islamabad. On the screen at the front of the auditorium, a Chinese rocket carrying Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, Pakistan’s first astronaut, rose on a column of orange flames. As the rocket lifted off, Pakistan’s national anthem began. The audience, which had been slouching in their seats, rose row by row and sang along. While many took out their phones to record the historic moment, Zainab Abbasi’s eyes remained fixed on the giant screen. “I had my phone out to record it on video, but I was so caught up in the moment that I forgot to record, and I was just standing there with my phone closed,” Abbasi, 21, told Al Jazeera. A second-year undergraduate student of physics and astronomy at the National University of Sciences and Technology (NUST), Abbasi was with her friends in the auditorium at the headquarters of the Pakistan Space & Upper Atmosphere Research Commission (SUPARCO). As the rocket climbed higher, the hall erupted in applause and chants of “Pakistan Zindabad” (“Long live Pakistan”). The Long March-2F rocket lifted off from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Centre in northwest China, carrying Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo and Wu Yi, alongside Ali, a 40-year-old Pakistan Air Force pilot. But within two minutes of liftoff, the hall fell silent. No one spoke. Faces across the rows were tense. On the screen, the rocket had shrunk to a dot. “There was, I think, anticipation and also, for me specifically, a sort of, you know, underlying anxiety,” Abbasi told Al Jazeera. On January 28, 1986, the US space shuttle Challenger broke apart 73 seconds after liftoff, killing all seven crew members. About 10 minutes after Wednesday’s launch, the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft separated from the rocket and entered orbit, according to the China Manned Space Agency (CMSA). The silence lasted several minutes, until one of the hosts congratulated the audience on a successful launch. People got up, greeted one another or headed for the doors. A few hours later, CMSA and SUPARCO confirmed that the spacecraft had docked at China’s Tiangong space station at 8:56am (03:56 GMT). After the AI chipmaker Nvidia announced it was bringing back embattled former head Jensen Huang and the company's stock shot up like a bullet, President Donald Trump took a very public victory lap. "I made the deal," he said during a lengthy phone interview with cable business news channel CNBC. Trump followed that with an AI-generated image posted to his social media platform that riffed on the famous photograph taken moments after the 2024 attempt on his life in Pennsylvania. But instead of Trump in the image, Huang was the one surrounded by Secret Service guards. It depicted him in front of an Nvidia banner - with a raised fist clenching a red bra. The post was classic Trump – potentially offensive, yet still a bit opaque. Was Trump suggesting Huang survived a scandal – one that includes allegations of recklessly jeopardising US national security by consorting with a suspected Chinese spy – the way he had survived an assassin's bullet? Was the bra a celebration Huang's reported extramarital affairs? By replacing the US flag with an Nvidia standard, was he claiming that America and one of its largest, most powerful companies are one and the same? At the very least, the image underscores how inextricably linked Huang and Trump now are, with the fate of the former hinging on the successes and failures of the latter. The report said the ministry declared Sylvain persona non grata. Kim Yo Jong, one of Pyongyang’s top foreign policy officials, described the Swiss sanctions as an “open hostile act” and an infringement of the North’s sovereignty in her statement Tuesday. North Korea has closely aligned with Russia over the war in Ukraine, sending thousands of troops and large shipments of weapons in recent years to support Russian President Vladimir Putin’s full-scale invasion, possibly in exchange for aid and military technology transfers. BepiColombo was launched as a joint mission between the European Space Agency and the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency in October 2018. Since then, it has navigated its way toward Mercury. On Nov. 21, the spacecraft attached itself to Mercury's orbit. The maneuver started with a scheduled, brief loss of contact with the mission control team at the European Space Operations Center in Darmstadt, Germany, the ESA said in a news release. As BepiColombo passed over the planet, it fired four axial thrusters that slowed it enough to lock into Mercury's orbit. During this stage of the mission, the spacecraft came within 400 miles of Mercury's surface. The burn was supposed to last for about 37 minutes. But when the ESA team reestablished contact with BepiColombo, they found the maneuver had been interrupted, causing the spacecraft to enter safe mode, where nonessential activities are stopped. Analysis of trajectory data showed the spacecraft had only completed about 77% of the maneuver. "Upon finding Bepi in safe mode, it was like flipping a switch. Everybody was focused in understanding what had happened," ESA BepiColombo flight operations director Ignacio Tanco said in a statement. The glitch has been traced to a software issue involving attitude guidance and thruster control, the ESA said. The investigation into the error is continuing. Despite the error and the incomplete maneuver, ESA scientists were eventually able to confirm that BepiColombo had locked onto Mercury's orbit. It took six hours from the time the maneuver started to confirm that it had been successful, the ESA said. Scientists often start with a clear idea of what they want a protein to do. clusters.title: Credit card spending surges 20 pc to Rs 2.45 lakh crore in October amid festive season: RBI data
clusters.text: New Delhi: Credit card spending in India rose sharply in October as festive season purchases gathered pace ahead of Diwali as total transaction value climbed close to 20 per cent month-on-month to Rs 2.45 lakh crore, according to Reserve Bank of India (RBI) data.The spending increase came after credit card transactions amounted to Rs 2.04 lakh crore in September and were also 14.4 per cent higher than the corresponding month last year that highlighted continued strength in consumer spending.Banks collectively added 14 lakh new credit cards in October, taking the industry's outstanding card base to 12.67 crore, compared with 12.53 crore in September.Digital channels continued to dominate spending patterns.Transactions through online and e-commerce platforms reached Rs 1.54 lakh crore, accounting for nearly 63 per cent of total credit card spending, while point-of-sale (PoS) transactions stood at Rs 90,562 crore.The country's largest card issuer, HDFC Bank, retained its lead in terms of spending volume with card transactions worth Rs 70,115 crore during the month which reflects a 7.6 per cent sequential increase.However, among major issuers, SBI Card and ICICI Bank also posted stronger growth.SBI Card recorded spending of Rs 45,797 crore, up 31 per cent from September, while ICICI Bank saw transaction value rise 37 per cent to Rs 42,295 crore.Axis Bank reported credit card spending of Rs 30,211 crore, registering a 30.5 per cent month-on-month increase.In addition, the number of credit card transactions rose 32 per cent year-on-year to 68.3 crore, outpacing growth in transaction value.However, average transaction size declined to around Rs 3,585 from Rs 4,133 a year earlier.The trend of growing usage of credit cards for smaller-ticket purchases, including transactions routed through RuPay credit cards linked to the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) which has expanded the use of credit cards in everyday payments.

clusters.text: Jannik Sinner attended a ceremony for players who had become world number one at the ATP Finals in Turin World number two Jannik Sinner says he has had "minor surgery" on his knee, just seven weeks before January's Australian Open begins. The five-time Grand Slam champion has not played competitively since winning Wimbledon on 12 July. In a post on Instagram, Sinner said he had undergone surgery to "improve the condition of my iliotibial band" - a thick band of tissue that runs along the outside of the knee. "Over the past few months, together with my team we've tried everything to treat my injury without surgery," the 25-year-old wrote. In a video posted on his Youtube channel in October, Sinner said he had also lost "a lot of weight" after having his tonsils removed. He also described having "days where I felt nothing and could play without any problems, and then days where I couldn't move at all". clusters.text: Ranchi/Jamshedpur: The Sikh community in Ranchi, Jamshedpur and the rest of the state celebrated Guru Nanak Dev’s 557th birth anniversary with prayers, nagar kirtan and langar on Tuesday.At Guru Nanak Higher Secondary School in Ranchi, a special diwan was organised. The 18-ft-high Palki Sahib was a major attraction.Six Gatka groups showcased Sikh martial art, while dastar-tying groups, religious organisations, social groups and schoolchildren participated. clusters.text: Jharkhand Health Minister Irfan Ansari has urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to cap airfares and curb what he called arbitrary fare increases by airlines, news agency Press Trust of India reported.Ansari also sought concessional fares for patients and family members accompanying them during emergencies, along with greater transparency in how ticket prices are determined.In a letter to the Prime Minister, the minister cited the case of a Jharkhand woman who could not afford a flight to visit her critically ill husband, who was undergoing treatment for a kidney ailment in Chandigarh."I was travelling to Delhi from Ranchi to attend an event organised by the Jharkhand Cabinet at the Bharat Mandapam. I was shocked to see that the fare from Ranchi to Delhi was around Rs 31,000. The Jharkhand government will cover my travel expenses, but what about that middle-class family for whom even raising such a large sum is difficult?"The minister said he was deeply pained to see the woman crying at the airport because of the high fare."Upon enquiry, it was learnt that her husband is battling a serious kidney ailment in Chandigarh. His condition is extremely critical. He had expressed a final wish: to see his wife one last time," Ansari said in the letter.Ansari said he arranged a ticket for the woman so that she could reach her husband. "At a time when a family needs the support of others the most, why should airline companies take advantage of their desperate situation and charge exorbitant fares?" he asked.Urging immediate action, Ansari wrote: "Prime Minister, I earnestly urge you to issue strict instructions to the minister of civil aviation immediately and establish a set of regulations regarding airfares. A maximum limit should be set for airfares."He added that sudden fare increases by airlines should be controlled. "Transparency in fare determination must be ensured, and strict action should be taken against the arbitrary practices of companies," Ansari said, according to PTI.Ansari's letter called on the Centre to set an upper limit for airfares, prevent sudden price increases and introduce concessional tickets for patients and accompanying family members during emergencies.- EndsMust Watch
